subject: Taxes
title: The Tipping Point Pattern
description: A quick, practical guide to The Tipping Point Pattern.

hook.text: The WhatsApp tax, the metro fare, the tea tax—tiny amounts triggered massive revolts.

buildup.text: Behavioral economists call it 'threshold theory.' People endure rising grievances until one small event breaks the dam.

discovery.text: The trigger is always symbolic. It represents everything unfair that came before.

twist.text: Governments focus on the trigger—cancel the tax—but miss the accumulated anger. That's why protests often continue.

climax.text: Smart tax policy addresses underlying grievances. Canceling the last straw doesn't unload the camel.

punchline.text: The trigger is never the cause. Accumulated unfairness is.

quiz.question: Why do tax revolts often continue after the triggering tax is canceled?
